To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
genomic prediction within doubled-haploid libraries from landraces was promising for the prediction of line per se performance for seven agronomic traits.

genomic prediction (GP), a statistical approach that predicts the phenotypes of genotypes based on their DNA sequence, can be successfully applied to doubled haploid libraries (DHH) of maize landrace lines.

genomic prediction (GP), a tool for the efficient use of the genetic potential of maize landraceres for future breeding, is promising within a doubled-haploid library (DHL) but requires large training sets (N > 50 lines).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of GP methods for DHL from landrace germplasm and the assessment of the prospects for their application.
the prospects of genomic selection in maize landraces and the potential of doubled-haploid libraries as a resource for future maize breeding.
the development of genomic prediction (G) for maize breeding.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GP is not a promising approach to predict the performance of lines from a DHL library.
genomic prediction in maize doubled-haploid lines is promising, but requires a large training population.
GP is a promising tool for the genetic improvement of DHL from maize landraces, but only for very large and expensive DHL.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GP is not useful for DHL, but it is useful for EF lines, which can be used to predict the performance of lines in the DHL.
genomic prediction in a single DHL library with a large training set (N > 200) and a large number of lines (N > 500) is promising, whereas prediction between or among DHL libraries is not.
GP is promising within and between DHL, but the prospects of GP among combined DHL are limited.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GP within DHL is a promising approach to exploit the genetic diversity of landraces in breeding programs.
GP is promising within and between DHL, but the prospects are limited for GP among DHL.
GP is a promising approach to exploit the rich genetic diversity harboured in landraces for maize improvement.
